races.name: Guinness Irish EBF Nursery Handicap

runners_data.name: I Ready
runners_data.note: Clearly the most likely pace-setter stepping up to 7f for the first time; four starts all over 6f on Good ground suit the conditions, Paul Flynn's 3-from-22 in 14 days is modest, and racing from a prominent position is its natural style though the step in trip is the key unknown.
runners_data.comment: Fresh off a win 11 days ago, I Ready has experience of today's distance and going and arrives in form carrying 140 lb from stall 7; the main risk is that his three starts before that victory brought an eighth, fifth and sixth.

runners_data.name: Banks Of The Boyne
runners_data.note: Bumped up to 8f last time but returns to 6-7f range which looks more suitable; the fades-in-finish flag is significant for a 7f handicap, Wesley Joyce's claim could help preserve energy in transit but this horse needs to be closer to the pace than its style suggests.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts — second last time out but unplaced and eighth in the two prior runs — Banks Of The Boyne carries 139 lb from stall eight, and our rating of 68 leaves him well held against this field on current form.

runners_data.name: Bold Commander
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien-trained runner dropping back to 5-6f experience stepping to 7f here; placed twice at 5f on Good ground, the trip is an open question, and Jack Cleary's 5lb claim gives a weight edge that could compensate if the pace is steady enough to suit.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, Bold Commander does bring going and distance experience to the table, and that second two starts back shows he can mix it at this level; the fifth last time out, however, suggests he's one to approach with caution from stall 4 off 139 lb.

runners_data.name: Seven Nation Army
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's hold-up type whose best recent finish was a second over 6f on Good; the 8f run last time suggests O'Brien has been searching for a trip and 7f may suit better, but needs a stronger pace than this field is likely to generate to deliver late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Seven Nation Army showed signs of life with a runner-up finish last time out, 11 days ago — fitness isn't an issue. He has experience of today's trip and going, and a trainer firing at 28%, though stall one and 137 lb are notable factors.

runners_data.name: Margot Mae
runners_data.note: Scott McCullagh rides a filly with a 7f placed effort (3rd, Good/Soft) already on the card; her prominent style fits this race shape well, and Mrs Harrington's runner carries the best distance profile in the field relative to the race conditions — straightforward tactical fit.
runners_data.comment: Margot Mae showed her best when third two starts back, and having run over today's trip and going, she arrives here fresh on 21 days' rest carrying 136 lb from stall three; winless in her last three, but her rating of 90 marks her as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Celtic Moon
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good last time and steps back in trip here; Ben Coen is a strong booking for J P Murtagh, and the 1W1P in similar going is encouraging — the drop to 7f from a winning 8f run could mean she has extra gears if the pace is right.
runners_data.comment: Celtic Moon arrives on the back of a win last time out, has experience of today's trip and conditions, and her rating of 85 suggests she's well treated; the sole concern is a trainer who has drawn a blank in 23 attempts over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Eighteenth Smiles
runners_data.note: Consistent 5th-place finisher at 6f, Joseph Patrick O'Brien second string here; the 'p' headgear flag is worth noting for a hold-up type that has yet to win in four starts — needs the race to fall apart late, which this pace map makes unlikely.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Eighteenth Smiles nevertheless brings strong fitness from 19 days ago, has run over today's trip and going, and a trainer firing at 28% makes him a live threat — though another unplaced effort last time is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Winnie's Wish
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's runner holds a substantial OR drop to 58 and is a genuine rear-runner by profile; though mapped to midfield due to field congestion, she will naturally seek cover at the back — the fades-in-finish flag alongside a 33-day absence and OR 58 make this a very difficult ask at 7f Galway.
runners_data.comment: Winnie's Wish has been well beaten in each of his last three starts, including two eighths, and ranked bottom on our figures here, he is hard to fancy at the weights; the trainer's recent strike rate offers little encouragement either, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: I Ready is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press from the outside, is expected to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over Galway's 7f on Good ground. Margot Mae and Celtic Moon are the most likely prominent horses to sit just behind, with Bold Commander and Banks Of The Boyne tracking in the early stages, but none carries the pace profile to challenge I Ready for the lead. This race shape — one front-runner controlling tempo with a modest pace cluster behind — classically favours horses who can sit close to the pace and quicken through the final two furlongs without being exposed by a sprint they cannot sustain. Winnie's Wish is a true hold-up horse whose redistribution to midfield reflects the congestion of similar types in the rear; she is unlikely to find a naturally comfortable position and her chance is tempered accordingly. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers who can travel handily in second or third and accelerate over the final furlong hold the structural advantage in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If I Ready dictates a comfortable, uncontested pace and the prominent group tracks efficiently throughout.
scenarios.body: I Ready sets a sustainable tempo that neither falls flat nor burns off the field, allowing horses like Celtic Moon and Margot Mae to travel smoothly and challenge off the home turn; the winner will most likely come from the leading group within two lengths at the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely modest and I Ready steals an unassailable advantage without the field realising until too late.
scenarios.body: A tardy response from the chasing pack — possible given multiple horses unfamiliar with this trip or in their first nursery campaign — means I Ready has enough daylight turning for home to hold on under Holohan; the gap to the prominent bunch never fully closes.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Get In Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than expected and the leaders tie up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Seven Nation Army and Eighteenth Smiles, both genuine hold-up types on their form profiles, would benefit if the tempo is hot enough to string out the field and leave an opening on the rail or outer late; this scenario is structurally dependent on a pace that this field's makeup makes unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is stop-start and a false pace produces a blanket finish in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Jostling for position among several horses with uncertain trip stamina at 7f — notably Banks Of The Boyne stepping back in and Bold Commander shortening up from sprint distances — could produce a messy, compressed finish where the widest-drawn, freshest horse gets a run; this scenario is low-probability given the relative clarity of I Ready's lead role.

watchPoints.text: Watch I Ready's sectionals in the opening furlong — if Holohan pushes forward uncontested and clears by two lengths before the 5f pole, the field may already be chasing a lost cause given the modest pace potential of the chasers.

Celtic Moon is stepping back from an 8f win to 7f; if Ben Coen settles her too far back in the early stages to conserve energy, she risks failing to close on a controlled front-runner — position off the break is critical.

Banks Of The Boyne is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish; at 7f with a return from 8f, Wesley Joyce must decide early whether to commit to the pace or drop in — neither option looks clean given the fading tendency.

Seven Nation Army and Eighteenth Smiles are both genuine hold-up types who need a true pace to fire; with only one front-runner in the field, watch whether either drifts wider than ideal looking for a gap that a modest gallop will not create.

Winnie's Wish's 33-day absence and OR 58 in a field rated up to 82 makes her a significant outsider; watch for Chris Hayes to find cover early — if she is caught wide at any point in the first half, her chance is effectively gone.

runners_data.name: Celtic Motif
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner, likely to go unchallenged to the lead; recent win over 8f on good ground for in-form O'Brien yard and cheekpieces suggest she'll be switched on — the key question is whether she can sustain it over 7f against a classier listed field.|
runners_data.comment: Celtic Motif won last time out and was second three starts back, showing consistent placed form in recent starts; she has run over today's trip and going, and a trainer firing at 28% adds stable confidence, though carrying 133 lb from stall 6 may test her.

runners_data.name: Goldilocks Cen
runners_data.note: Unquantified style makes pace profiling difficult; Archie Watson yard has had just one winner from 13 runs in the 14-day window and her recent form includes a win at 8f on soft followed by modest efforts, making her profile hard to trust at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten in her last two outings and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Goldilocks Cen is hard to fancy despite carrying a manageable weight from stall five; a win three starts back hints at ability, and she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Greydreambeliever
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who has placed repeatedly at 7f on good ground — five of her last ten runs at 7f on good produced two places — and Declan McDonogh has a strong record riding off the pace at Galway; needs a pace scenario that creates a gap.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Greydreambeliever is hard to fancy despite the second two starts back — though she has experience over today's trip and going, and a trainer firing at 28% is worth noting.

runners_data.name: La Brodeuse
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who placed last time over 7f on good ground at this level, and Kevin Ryan's yard has had no winners from 21 runners in the past fortnight, which is a mild concern; will need a clean run in the prominent pack where traffic danger is highest.|
runners_data.comment: La Brodeuse ran second two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with a rating of 104 suggesting she retains ability — but a trainer who is yet to land one in 21 attempts over the past fortnight is a concern, and she arrives 54 days fresh.

runners_data.name: Nancy J
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type with a placed record at 7f on good ground and Ben Coen's patient Galway rides are worth noting; has the profile to finish strongly if the prominent pack causes its own problems, though her last three runs have been modest.|
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and third again four starts back, Nancy J shows consistency without ever threatening the top spot in recent starts — she's yet to win in her last five. Experience over today's trip and going helps, but a trainer in a cold spell and 133 lb from stall one are factors to weigh.

runners_data.name: Noli Timere
runners_data.note: Has won twice on good ground but is a genuine prominent racer who cannot secure that position in this field shape; effectively racing out of role in midfield, which structurally reduces her chance regardless of her ability — her style-fit discount is real here.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of ten on our figures, Noli Timere faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns after 50 days fresher than when last seen finishing fifth.

runners_data.name: Black Caviar Gold
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 103 alongside Meriden, placed twice over 8f on good ground and her headgear (tongue-tie/cheekpieces) suggests she needs to be prominent and switched on early; two runs at 7f on good showing she handles the trip well.|

runners_data.name: Meriden
runners_data.note: Six-race winning streak including four consecutive wins at 7f-8f on good ground is the standout form in the race; Chris Hayes is a powerful ally and her natural prominent style is perfectly matched to this race shape — the class and consistency metrics point firmly to her.|

runners_data.name: Pivotal Attack
runners_data.note: Naturally wants to race prominently but is mapped to midfield given the congestion ahead of her; has placed at 7f on good ground but racing out of role and with a trainer returning 0 wins from 5 runners in 14 days, her structural disadvantage here is significant.|
runners_data.comment: Pivotal Attack showed real promise with a third and a second in recent starts, and she has experience over today's trip and going; rated 109 by us, she shapes as a leading danger, though her fourth last time out raises questions about consistency.

races.paceDynamic: Celtic Motif is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse likely to lead, she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without being dragged into a speed duel. Celestial Orbit, La Brodeuse, Black Caviar Gold and Meriden all want to race prominently, creating a congested group tracking Celtic Motif through the first half, with real traffic danger two to three furlongs out as that pack compresses. Pivotal Attack and Noli Timere are natural prominent types who cannot all get their desired position in this configuration and have been mapped to midfield, meaning they will likely race out of role and their effectiveness is reduced. The field holds more prominent-running types than the race shape can accommodate — Celtic Motif is best placed to secure the front, with Meriden and Black Caviar Gold most likely to lock onto her directly — and the result is a race that should favour a well-placed prominent runner who can travel smoothly in the first three, attack from two furlongs out and sustain the effort on good ground without needing to produce a sudden burst from further back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Celtic Motif sets a honest but uncontested gallop and the prominent pack sits neatly behind without incident.
scenarios.body: Celtic Motif controls fractions, the well-placed prominent types (Meriden, Black Caviar Gold, Celestial Orbit) cruise into contention entering the final two furlongs and the smoothest traveller sustains the run to the line; the race suits horses who can race on the bridle in second or third and deliver a clean, progressive challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack gets too close too early and burns energy challenging Celtic Motif, leaving her to dictate and steal a march.
scenarios.body: With the prominent bunch spending themselves chasing Celtic Motif through the bend, she conserves enough to repel the challenge in the final furlong on good ground that suits her recent form; her trainer's in-form yard and her recent win over this trip and course profile support this outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply early as prominent runners jostle for position and the race becomes a true test of stamina.
scenarios.body: Traffic trouble in the prominent pack leaves Nancy J and Greydreambeliever able to thread through from midfield/hold-up positions as rivals tire, rewarding patience and a clear run in the final two furlongs; Nancy J's course form at 7f and Greydreambeliever's repeated placed efforts on good ground make them the likeliest beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Midrace
scenarios.trigger: If Celtic Motif sets too slow a pace early and the race turns into a sprint finish from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A false-pace scenario scrambles the field and advantages any prominent runner who has saved enough petrol, but with Pivotal Attack and Noli Timere racing out of their natural role their effectiveness here is structurally compromised; Meriden's electric recent form and finishing speed give her the best chance if the race devolves into a dash.

watchPoints.text: Prominent pack congestion between the 3f and 2f markers — Celestial Orbit, La Brodeuse, Black Caviar Gold and Meriden all want the same ground and a squeeze or check at the critical moment could end multiple horses' races instantly.

Celtic Motif's ability to hold off the prominent pack in the final furlong — if she has set a genuinely sustainable pace she becomes a live winning threat, but if the prominents absorb her too easily she could capitulate quickly.

Pivotal Attack and Noli Timere racing wide or taking unexpected positions as they seek to compensate for being pushed out of their natural prominent slot — both could cause interference for legitimate midfield runners like Nancy J.

Greydreambeliever's finishing run depends entirely on a clear passage late; with the prominent group packed tightly, a blocked rail or checked run at the 1f pole would cost her a placed chance that her form genuinely merits.

Meriden's in-running price — if she settles smoothly in second or third behind Celtic Motif through the first half, her unbeaten run at this trip on this ground means any drift outward or untidy jump should be taken as a warning sign of something amiss rather than opportunity.

races.name: Guinness Open Gate Brewery Novice Steeplechase (Grade 3)

runners_data.name: Shadow Paddy
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with four wins from five completed starts on Good ground and an outstanding turf record; the confirmed pace-setter here, but his front-running role means his STYLE_FIT flags a marginal out-of-role concern if rivals push him — though in this field he is almost certain to lead unchallenged.|

runners_data.name: Court Canyon
runners_data.note: Recent course-distance winner at Galway on Good gives him strong place claims, but he is a natural front-runner who is unlikely to secure that position ahead of Shadow Paddy and is effectively mapped to midfield; 87 days since last run is worth monitoring.|

runners_data.name: Le Coq Hardi
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's in-form yard (6/39 past 14 days), horse has won and placed at 20f on Good at Galway and handles this trip well; sits in a genuine prominent berth and his course-and-distance reliability makes him a significant force in the dominant scenario.|

runners_data.name: Soir De Garde
runners_data.note: Paul Townend in the saddle for Mullins is always a factor; a natural prominent type pushed toward the rear in the mapping, though his winning form on Good and recent return to form give him credibility if the race develops into a stamina examination late on.|

runners_data.name: Wild Bill Hickok
runners_data.note: Four-year-old whose age profile suggests upside, and he won at 16f on Good as recently as 52 days ago; sits in a genuine prominent position on the map and could prove well-treated at OR 135 if he jumps cleanly throughout.|

runners_data.name: Lady Bluebird
runners_data.note: Consistent mare with three wins from 15 runs on similar going and good Galway form at this trip; a natural front-runner whose style has been redistributed to midfield in this crowded pace scenario — her actual racing pattern means she will want to be closer than the map shows.|

runners_data.name: Queenofthelodge
runners_data.note: Only eight days since her last run following a winning effort, which makes the quick turnaround notable; like Lady Bluebird she is a front-runner by nature pushed into a midfield slot on the map, so her ability to settle off the pace in a real race is an open question.|

races.paceDynamic: Shadow Paddy is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with seven runners over 2m2f on Good ground, is very likely to dictate from the front at a sustainable gallop without serious pressure. Le Coq Hardi and Wild Bill Hickok are the two horses most likely to track Shadow Paddy in genuine prominent positions, while Court Canyon, Lady Bluebird, and Queenofthelodge are all naturally prominent types who cannot all occupy that territory and are effectively pushed back into a midfield cluster. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Shadow Paddy is almost certain to lead, with Le Coq Hardi the most credible challenger for second position given trainer De Bromhead's excellent recent form and the horse's course-distance profile. A controlled, single-paced gallop set by Shadow Paddy favours horses who can travel prominently without burning energy fighting for position, making confirmed prominent stalkers and those who handle a steady-then-quicken finish the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shadow Paddy Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Shadow Paddy leads uncontested at a measured clip and the race becomes a test of jumping efficiency and a late burst.
scenarios.body: Shadow Paddy sets a comfortable tempo over the fences and the race only ignites from two out, rewarding horses who have tracked closely and conserved energy throughout; Le Coq Hardi, positioned just off the pace with superior course form, and Wild Bill Hickok, whose fresh-legged profile suits a race run to suit prominent racers, are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Grind Test
scenarios.trigger: If Shadow Paddy's lead becomes so comfortable that the gallop dies completely and the race turns into a stamina slog from the third-last.
scenarios.body: A near-crawl suits horses with deep reserves of stamina over this 2m2f trip; Soir De Garde, trained by Mullins and dropping back having won over shorter, and Lady Bluebird, whose good-ground form figures are consistent, could pick up the pieces from a closer position than their mapped placement suggests.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Ignites Early
scenarios.trigger: If the natural front-running instincts of Court Canyon or Queenofthelodge override their mapped positions and they push Shadow Paddy into a genuinely contested gallop.
scenarios.body: A hotter pace filters out the horses shuffled back involuntarily and rewards those who travel fluently at speed over fences; Wild Bill Hickok, only four years old and unencumbered by a fight for position, and Le Coq Hardi, proven over course and distance on Good, have the scope to handle an honest pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Capitalise Late
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or a mid-race surge strings the field out and the horses mapped toward the rear find daylight in the straight.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on redistributed prominent types — Queenofthelodge and Lady Bluebird — acting as genuine hold-up horses, which is contrary to their natural style, making this the least likely outcome; only if both stumble through the early fences and are forced back does this shape have any real merit.

watchPoints.text: Shadow Paddy's jumping must be monitored from the first fence — any error at the head of affairs on Good ground could immediately disrupt the entire race shape and compress the field behind him.

Court Canyon, Lady Bluebird, and Queenofthelodge are all natural front-runners; watch the first two furlongs to see whether any attempt to push past Shadow Paddy and convert this into a genuinely contested gallop rather than the expected controlled procession.

Wild Bill Hickok is only four years old tackling a field of older, more experienced novice chasers — watch his jumping particularly at the downhill fences where greenness could cost him ground or position.

Soir De Garde carries the Mullins-Townend combination and was beaten less than three lengths last time out — if he travels more fluently than his redistributed map position suggests, he could emerge as a late threat from the second-last fence onward.

races.name: Guinness Novice Hurdle

runners_data.name: Flying Ace
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's five-year-old arrives in excellent form with three successive wins on Good ground at around this trip, but as a natural prominent racer in a field stuffed with similar types, Kevin Healy (claiming 7lb) may find the early positions more contested than ideal, tempering confidence despite the strong form line.

runners_data.name: Midnight Jet
runners_data.note: The only horse in the race whose lead role is uncontested; Henry De Bromhead's five-year-old has won at Galway on Good ground and showed courage when fifth in a Grade 1, and Darragh O'Keeffe will simply be able to bowl along from the off with no pressure forcing a false pace.

runners_data.name: Brother Walfrid
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy's mount won last time on Good at 19f and carries the tongue-tie, but as another Elliott prominent type in a yard already represented by Flying Ace, he is likely to find his natural front-end berth cut off and will need to adapt his racing style mid-race.

runners_data.name: Look Sport
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's five-year-old has just the one run to his name — a win on Good going — but that single-run profile is difficult to assess in a novice of this depth; Sean Flanagan's mount is naturally a prominent racer shown at the rear purely through redistribution, meaning the hold-up tag does not reflect his likely race behaviour.

runners_data.name: Luker's Tipple
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's gelding ran only 16 days ago and was a narrow winner over 2m on Good, giving him a freshness edge, and Keith Donoghue will need a clear run from midfield; his sim-going record shows one win from 15 comparable-ground starts, which raises a small concern about consistency despite recent form.

runners_data.name: Roc Dino
runners_data.note: Paul Townend partners the Mullins horse who won over 22f on Good ground last time — the longest-distance win in this field — and while his soft-ground form is mixed, the return to Good going at a longer trip suits; he is the natural second-string prominent type whose race-craft allows him to slot in behind Midnight Jet without the positional fight the others face.

runners_data.name: Rosie's Wings
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's mare landed a 16f win on Good at her most recent start with Danny Gilligan, but her entire recent form is built around two-mile trips at Galway, and all five of her comparable-ground runs are on Good, suggesting the step to 2m4½f — combined with being forced wide of her preferred prominent spot — is a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Siege Of Carthage
runners_data.note: Josh Halley's six-year-old is a progressive type who won over 20f on Good and finished second at 18f on Heav, and Phillip Enright regularly partners him; the horse steps up in trip having already shown he handles a Galway test, and his straightforward prominent style sits comfortably within the available race positions without the redistribution pressure others face.

races.paceDynamic: Midnight Jet is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner novice hurdle over 2m4½f at Galway on Good ground, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, he is poised to dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo from the outset. The pace map is congested behind him: Flying Ace, Brother Walfrid, Luker's Tipple, Rosie's Wings, and Look Sport are all natural prominent racers, meaning several will be forced to race out of their preferred position, creating a scrappy battle for the prominent slots in the early stages. Roc Dino and Siege Of Carthage appear the most likely to settle in their natural rhythm without fighting for position, giving them a tactical advantage in what could become a messy race behind the leader. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Midnight Jet is almost certain to lead, with Flying Ace and Roc Dino (both with strong Good-ground form) best placed to secure the prominent positions closest to him. The race shape firmly favours a well-organised prominent racer who can travel smoothly close to Midnight Jet's controlled pace and quicken from the second-last, rather than a hold-up horse forced to navigate traffic generated by the reshuffling pack.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Midnight Jet Controls, Quickens Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Midnight Jet bowls along at a fair but unhurried pace and kicks decisively from the second-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: Midnight Jet has won at Galway on Good ground and is unchallenged for the lead, giving Henry De Bromhead's lightly-framed five-year-old every chance to dictate on his own terms with Darragh O'Keeffe allowing him to travel kindly. With no pressure applied early, he arrives at the final two hurdles full of running and his 2m4½f form profile strongly suits this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Runs Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just slow enough that a horse travelling prominently behind Midnight Jet builds momentum approaching the last and overpowers him on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Flying Ace's four wins at around this trip on Good ground make him the most credible threat if he can secure a clean prominent berth despite the congestion, and Roc Dino's Mullins/Townend combination will be intent on getting cover just off the pace before a well-timed run. The Good ground and Galway's stiff finish reward horses with stamina allied to a turn of foot, and either of these two could wear down Midnight Jet in the final 150 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Creates Late Rush
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling for prominent positions burns off several horses and opens the race up for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: The volume of natural front-runners redistributed to midfield means scrimmaging in the first mile is plausible, and if Midnight Jet's tempo quickens to absorb those fighting for position, the whole field could arrive in a cluster at the second-last. Siege Of Carthage won over 2m on Good ground at this track and, if given a clear passage late, has the profile to capitalise; Look Sport is a one-time winner on Good going but is mapped at the rear entirely out of natural role, so genuine late momentum is limited.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Stragglers Profit
scenarios.trigger: If several prominent horses over-race early in the fight for position, tire badly, and the race falls apart in the straight.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given Midnight Jet's ability to control tempo from the front without a challenger, but if early carnage in the chasing pack produces a truly ragged race, a horse fresh off a recent run — Luker's Tipple ran just 16 days ago and won over 2m on Good — could benefit from a loose-run situation. Rosie's Wings similarly won last time on Good ground but her natural prominent style is compromised by the redistribution, making this scenario heavily dependent on circumstances rather than design.

watchPoints.text: Midnight Jet — if Darragh O'Keeffe is foot-perfect at the first two hurdles and immediately establishes a clear lead, the race could be over as a contest by the time the field reaches the home turn.

Flying Ace — watch how Kevin Healy (7lb claim) handles the immediate scramble for prominent positions; if he is forced back into the chasing pack in the first half-mile, his effectiveness is significantly reduced despite strong recent form.

Roc Dino — the Mullins/Townend combination will seek the position immediately behind Midnight Jet, and if they get it cleanly, Roc Dino's superior stamina profile at 22f gives him an edge in the straight that the market may not fully reflect.

Look Sport — Sean Flanagan's mount is shown at the rear purely as an artefact of redistribution; watch whether Flanagan pushes forward from the outset to reclaim a prominent position, which would add to early crowding and could unsettle the pace behind Midnight Jet.

Luker's Tipple — a 16-day turnaround can be a positive sign from Gavin Cromwell but watch his early movement at the start; if he settles kindly mid-pack he is in the race, but if he over-races in the congestion he may not see out the extra quarter-mile.

races.name: Guinness Galway Hurdle Handicap (Grade 3)

runners_data.name: Solness
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner under J J Slevin for O'Brien, racing with tongue-tie and cheekpieces; proven on good ground over this trip and the key pace influence, though at OR 153 he carries top weight and must be respected as a potential winner if he controls the tempo from the front — style fit is high for his role here.
runners_data.comment: Solness arrives here just 11 days after a placed effort — third last time out and a runner-up two starts back — showing he's in consistent form, and he has experience of today's trip and going. With a trainer firing at 28%, he's the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Casheldale Lad
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for Gordon Elliott returning from 213 days off with a new jockey (5lb claimer Josh Williamson), but has strong form at this distance on good ground; a genuine prominent racer who is well-placed to secure one of the limited early berths and could be tightened up by the long layoff.
runners_data.comment: Casheldale Lad arrives here as a double winner in recent starts, and has run over today's trip and going — giving him a solid profile at 165 lb off an official mark of 152. The sole concern is a fall two starts back, though a close third last time suggests confidence is intact.

runners_data.name: Ndaawi
runners_data.note: Won his last start on good going over 2m, trained by Gordon Elliott, and a prominent type who should get a decent position in running; the dip to 2m from slightly longer trips suits, though his soft-ground form is weak and recent good-ground form gives genuine encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Ndaawi bounces back from an unplaced run with a win on his latest start, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions, making him a genuine threat at 165 lb; the 60-day absence is the one query.

runners_data.name: El Cairos
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes over on this 143-rated Elliott six-year-old who has solid course-and-distance profile; drawn into a prominent role that suits, though form reads slightly inconsistently and a few below-par efforts at higher OR levels need explaining before confidence levels peak.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out and fifth two starts back give El Cairos a modest recent profile, but a win three starts back shows he retains ability. He has experience over today's trip and going, though 93 days off the track is a fitness query at 156 lb.

runners_data.name: Laafi
runners_data.note: William Durkan's prominent-style six-year-old showed up well on good ground last time (second at OR 143 over 2m), but his trainer has no runners in the past 14 days and the soft-ground record is a red flag; if conditions remain good he is at least worth including in the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out, with a disqualification before that muddying the waters, Laafi has run over today's trip and going and our rating of 150 marks him out as a serious contender; the main concern is 82 days off the track carrying 156 lb.

runners_data.name: Puturhandstogether
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden is a notable booking for O'Brien's five-year-old but recent form is deeply unconvincing — four consecutive out-of-the-first-six finishes including a 16th — and the OR of 140 may flatter current ability; prominent style is unlikely to translate into a meaningful position in this deep field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a second four starts back the lone highlight in a patchy recent sequence, Puturhandstogether returns after 44 days off carrying 153 lb; has run over today's trip and going, and a trainer firing at 28% offers some hope.

runners_data.name: Tounsivator
runners_data.note: Ran just three days ago and that minimal recovery time is the dominant concern for Danny Mullins and Mullins stable, even though the horse has excellent good-ground form (two wins at the trip) and a very clean record on going-to-firm; fitness may trump race shape here as the biggest risk factor.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and returning on just three days' rest, Tounsivator faces a stiff ask carrying 152 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 145 suggests he holds residual ability in a big field.

runners_data.name: Murcia
runners_data.note: Paul Townend rides this 138-rated Mullins five-year-old who is a genuine front-runner by nature — won last on good going over 2m — but the overcrowded pace scenario pushes him back in the map; if Townend can engineer a position closer than predicted, his good-ground form makes him a live contender, but he may be racing further back than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Ran to some effect last time out with a second, and a winner two starts back keeps her profile alive, though she carries a hefty 151 lb and ranks seventh of 21 on our rating; has run over today's trip and going, but patchy recent form is the concern.

runners_data.name: Too Bossy For Us
runners_data.note: Mark Walsh and Mullins with a five-year-old who ran three days ago, and consistency flags as a concern — six finishes of 6th across varied distances; the prominent style in theory suits but the form string doesn't inspire confidence that a small reduction in OR gets him competitive here.
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner four starts back but has pulled up since and was beaten again three days ago; he has run over today's trip and the 151 lb burden won't help him make his way back from the top of that recent slide.

runners_data.name: Helvic Dream
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old for Noel Meade returning from 88 days, with his true nature as a prominent racer squeezed out of that position in this field; his most recent form figures are all double-digit finishes on going worse than good, and the form on genuinely good ground dates back, making him a tough sell in this company.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, though a second three starts back offers some encouragement; he has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 143 suggests he holds ability. The 88-day absence and 149 lb burden are the key concerns.

runners_data.name: Starting Fifteen
runners_data.note: E McNamara's five-year-old returns from 111 days with a promising OR-135 rating and won over this trip on heavy at Hexham; naturally wants to race prominently but will be forced further back than ideal — his two good-ground runs show modest figures and the layoff adds another layer of doubt.
runners_data.comment: Starting Fifteen landed a win three starts back and was second four starts back, but fifth last time out suggests he returns here out of form; has run over today's trip and going, though 111 days off the track and 148 lb to carry are notable hurdles.

runners_data.name: Gameball
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's six-year-old has a genuinely strong recent form profile (won twice at OR around 133 on good ground over 2m) and Brian Hayes could be a key booking; pushed into a midfield slot despite being a front-to-prominent type, but if he can find a workable position he is among the more compelling form entries in the race.
runners_data.comment: Consistent enough in recent starts, with a win four starts back and another five starts back, but he hasn't converted in his last three outings — a fourth, third, and runner-up. Has run over today's trip and going, and returns fit on 20 days' rest, though 146 lb is a stern burden.

runners_data.name: Ragmans Corner
runners_data.note: Won last time out at OR 132 over 2m1f on good ground, trained by the small yard of Gerard Keane — a potential improver at a realistic mark; like several others here he is a front-runner squeezed back, but his recent winning form and light weight give him a place in any shortlist despite the positional challenge.
runners_data.comment: Ragmans Corner won last time out and has distance and going experience in his favour, but ranked 19 of 21 on our figures he faces a stiff task here; 67 days off the track adds another question mark for the handicapper to weigh up.

runners_data.name: Putapoundinthejar
runners_data.note: Won last on good ground for A J Martin and carries only 142lbs — one of the lighter weights in the field; a consistent prominent type who faces the same issue as other natural front-runners in this pack, but his form is freshly minted and the reduced weight is a meaningful physical advantage.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 17 of 21 on our figures, Putapoundinthejar faces a stiff ask under 142 lb, and his recent form is patchy — third and fifth in the two starts before that, though he does arrive on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Beauvallon
runners_data.note: Brian Hayes in the plate for Mullins on a lightly-raced four-year-old (OR 132) who holds a genuine hold-up style — this is the natural architectural fit for the predicted race shape; won on soft but ran well on good last time (second at 17f), and youth allied to a low weight and proper late-running style makes him one of the most profile-compliant horses in the race.
runners_data.comment: Beauvallon has winning form in recent starts — a winner two starts back and again three starts back — but ranked bottom of the field on our figures, he faces a stiff task conceding weight all round off 141 lb, despite arriving fit and with experience of today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Sageborough
runners_data.note: Won last on good ground over 2m1f for Paul Nolan and has a tongue-tie on; classed as a prominent type, but squeezed back among the midfield group in this shape — his winning form is recent and the going suits, so if he can ride the race patiently he remains dangerous despite not naturally finishing from behind.
runners_data.comment: Sageborough bounced back to winning ways last time out, but his last-five record is mixed — a fall and two out-of-the-money finishes among them — and 64 days off plus 141 lb make confidence hard to hold at a handicap mark of 128.

runners_data.name: Royal Hollow
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's eight-year-old ran just 22 days ago and showed up placing form on good and soft; another natural prominent racer displaced by the numbers game, but this horse's most recent form includes three consecutive places at the trip and he should not be entirely dismissed simply because of positional challenges.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 18 of 21 on our figures, Royal Hollow is hard to fancy despite a lively recent profile. She was a winner three starts back, and third two starts back, but 140 lb is a stern ask, and her rating of 127 leaves her well behind the top weights on paper; distance and going experience at least gives her a fair footing.

runners_data.name: Barbizon
runners_data.note: Four-year-old for Gordon Elliott ridden by a 7lb claimer, carrying 140lbs and with a hold-up style that fits the dominant race shape well; lightly raced over hurdles (one win at 2m on heavy), with modest turf form on good — the style is right but the class question needs answering.
runners_data.comment: Barbizon has experience of today's trip and conditions, and a win in his last five starts gives him a platform, but back-to-back unplaced efforts are a concern; the 140 lb burden does him no favours here.

runners_data.name: Kai Lung
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago for Mullins — ultra-short recovery time is the overriding concern — but the horse's hold-up style genuinely suits the predicted race shape and the 7lb claimer keeps the weight low; recent finishing position of 3rd over 2m on good (16 runs ago) shows he can handle the surface, but freshness is a real unknown.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up and unseated in two of his last four starts before a third last time out, Kai Lung arrives 65 days fresh and is hard to fancy ranked 15 of 21 on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going, and that sole recent win does at least show ability on a good day.

runners_data.name: Thisistheway
runners_data.note: Yvonne Latta's seven-year-old (no trainer strike rate in the past 14 days) is a prominent type mapped to midfield and carries 140lbs for a 5lb claimer; form includes placing at 2m+ on good but inconsistency and a fall in recent history make this a speculative inclusion in any scenario.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 20 of 21 on our figures, Thisistheway is hard to fancy despite experience over today's trip and going; she does boast a win in her last five starts — five starts back — but a fall and a fourth in more recent outings make her a tough sell here.

runners_data.name: No Looking Back
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 89 days off for Oliver McKiernan (0 from 3 in past 14 days) — the going is fine (tongue-tie and blinkers noted) but form figures are largely disappointing; the true hold-up profile suits the predicted race shape architecturally, yet the class level and trainer form do not give strong grounds for confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pulled up and two unplaced efforts among recent form, No Looking Back is hard to fancy ranked 16 of 21 on our figures; 89 days off adds to the concern, though a third two starts back and experience over today's trip and going offer slim encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Solness is the confirmed lone front-runner and, with just one genuine pace-setter in a 21-runner Grade 3 field, he is likely to dictate a controlled, measured gallop around Galway's undulating two miles, jumping fluently in front for Joseph O'Brien under J J Slevin. The going is good throughout the card, providing a fair surface that will not filter the field — stamina and tactical positioning will both matter, and with a single honest pace-setter setting a sustainable tempo, the race is unlikely to be a true test of finishing speed from the front but rather a strongly-run home straight where those settled in behind will be unleashed. The field holds substantially more genuine front-running and prominent types than can physically hold those positions — Murcia, Helvic Dream, Starting Fifteen, Gameball, Ragmans Corner, Putapoundinthejar, Sageborough, Royal Hollow and others are all natural front-to-prominent racers who will be squeezed back in the early stages, with Solness, Casheldale Lad, Ndaawi and El Cairos most likely to actually secure the prominent positions in running. This race shape clearly favours patient, well-handicapped hold-up and midfield types who can be delivered with one smooth run from two out — horses like Beauvallon, Kai Lung and Barbizon are architecturally suited, as are any redistributed prominent types comfortable sitting closer than usual if they settle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Solness Controls, Stays Honest
scenarios.trigger: If Solness bowls along at a fair but controlled pace and the prominent berths are limited to three or four horses, setting up a genuine gallop that rewards those delivered into contention from two out.
scenarios.body: Solness dictates a clean rhythm, the field strings out in the first mile, and those tucked just off the pace — or brought with a well-timed challenge — hit the rising ground at Galway in prime position; the pace is honest but not brutal, meaning true staying handicappers and class horses who settle well are the beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Solness goes faster than anticipated under pressure from runners who drift wide early, creating a genuinely strong pace that unravels the prominent types.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop stretches the field, Solness fades between the last two flights, and genuine hold-up horses who have been motoring through beaten rivals from the rear find themselves with momentum and space; this is the shape that most rewards deep closers dropped out in the early stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the race is a touch slowly run early and Murcia or Gameball manage to secure a closer position than their redistributed placement suggests, allowing front-runners-in-disguise to dominate from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A modest gallop means horses forced back from their natural positions are still travelling sweetly rounding the bend; those with the engine to sprint from three out, rather than grind home, benefit enormously, and the race develops into a tactical contest won in the final two flights.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In The Pack
scenarios.trigger: If the large 21-runner field produces jumping errors or interference in midfield, fragmenting the race into groups and creating a lottery in the straight.
scenarios.body: Fallers or untidy leaps disrupt the rhythm of several midfielders, the race splits into two or three distinct groups on the final climb, and a horse who has tracked the front-runner cleanly — or one who is produced late and wide — benefits from having clean air throughout.

watchPoints.text: Beauvallon and Kai Lung are the two cleanest architectural fits for the dominant shape — watch whether Brian Hayes drops Beauvallon in early and can find a clear run from two out, as any switching or traffic problem in the straight could cost him the race.

Tounsivator (3 days) and Too Bossy For Us (3 days) both ran midweek — watch both in the parade ring for signs of fatigue or sweat before the off, as rapid back-up at Galway in a Grade 3 is a genuine stamina and freshness risk.

The 21-runner field creates significant jumping-interference danger from two miles of open company — watch the early fences for a pile-up among the prominent types fighting for position, particularly around Murcia, Gameball and Ragmans Corner who all want to be in the same three or four places.

races.name: Rockshore Refreshingly Irish Handicap

runners_data.name: Pink Oxalis
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer for Stephen Thorne who showed a placed effort over 8f on Good recently, though the consistent habit of finishing mid-pack (recent form 003562) and a 3lb claimer aboard makes a winning surge from the back harder to envisage in a field this congested.
runners_data.comment: Pink Oxalis is our top-rated runner in a field of 17, and her second last time out — returned quickly after just 11 days — shows she's heading the right way. Winless in her last six, the weight of 140 lb from stall 12 is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Tolebi
runners_data.note: Nicola Burns takes the 5lb claim for Gerard O'Leary on this hold-up type who drops back from sprint distances, but three blanks on Good ground and zero wins in the last twelve months leaves the trip as a query and the form as uninspiring.
runners_data.comment: Tolebi has been knocking on the door, finishing fourth last time out and fourth again three starts back, and he has run over today's going before; 22 days between runs leaves him fit enough to threaten; the risk is he's yet to win in recent starts and that 137 lb burden could just blunt his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Hygge
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's in-form prominent racer won over 17f on Good last time out and carries strong recent course form; the drop back in trip to 1m½f is a logical targeting move and the T14 strike rate of 4/30 suggests Elliott's string is firing — one of the more compelling profiles in the field.
runners_data.comment: Rated well below his official mark on our figures and ranked near the foot of the field, Hygge is hard to fancy despite winning last time out; he has run over today's trip and going before, but 133 lb is a stiff ask for a horse rated this low on speed.

runners_data.name: Molto Amichi
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good most recently and placed over 9f on Soft, giving Luke McAteer a straightforward trip-and-going profile to exploit; the prominent style meshes perfectly with the expected race shape and the trainer sends this horse out fit off a 17-day break.
runners_data.comment: Molto Amichi arrives on the back of a win last time out, with a second two starts back suggesting he's been in decent nick recently, though a ninth three starts back hints at inconsistency; he has run over today's distance and going, and 133 lb from stall 5 makes life no easier.

runners_data.name: Vega's Muse
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, and while the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) notes this horse sometimes races off the pace, it is mapping to lead here — if it does so uncontested on Good ground over a flat 1m½f, it controls the pace narrative throughout, though Mrs Harrington's yard has been busy (3/34 T14) suggesting not peak form.
runners_data.comment: Vega's Muse showed she can win when landing the spoils four starts back, but her two most recent efforts have been disappointing, and at 133 lb from stall 9 she faces a stiff ask, though she has experience of today's trip and conditions.

runners_data.name: Exquisite Acclaim
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old hold-up type for Adrian McGuinness who wears a visor and has struggled to land a blow on Good ground (0W1P in similar conditions); the recent form string (040736) offers little encouragement, and 14 days between runs is straightforward.
runners_data.comment: Exquisite Acclaim showed a flash of form with a third two starts back, but he has been winless in his last six starts and that sixth last time out is a concern; experience over today's distance and going helps, though he faces a stiff task from stall 13 off 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Glyndwr
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the mount on this hold-up horse returning after just seven days, which could mean the O'Leary yard is confident; the best form shows a win at 8f on Standard and a third on Good over 9f, and the quick turnaround deserves a line through for market watchers.
runners_data.comment: Glyndwr shaped well with a third last time out, and a winner five starts back, he arrives on a quick seven-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going — the 131 lb burden is the one note of caution, but the overall profile makes him an appealing each-way proposition.

runners_data.name: Follow Me
runners_data.note: W J Lee partners this hold-up type for Ross O'Sullivan wearing a visor; the horse placed twice on Good at 10f recently but two blanks at 7-8f on Good and Soft suggest it needs a stronger gallop to bring its finishing effort to bear than Vega's Muse is likely to set.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Follow Me does at least return here with experience of today's trip and going, and that third last time out offers some encouragement; however, 129 lb from stall 16 makes life harder for a horse ranked sixth of seventeen.

runners_data.name: Earls
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's nine-year-old has run three consecutive seconds on Good ground over 8f — a remarkably consistent placed horse; true hold-up style pushed into midfield by field size, and Reese Holohan's 7lb claim partially offsets the OR disadvantage, though age and an absence of a win make it a place proposition.
runners_data.comment: Earls has been runner-up three times in recent starts yet remains winless, and a trainer striking at just 5% in the past fortnight is a concern; he has distance and going experience to draw on, though, and returns after 17 days off in reasonable shape on paper.

runners_data.name: Merlin The Wizard
runners_data.note: Two recent wins — over 10f and 12f on Good — give R P Cody's six-year-old the most compelling recent form in the race; a true hold-up type shuffled into midfield by traffic, raced just two days ago which is the shortest gap in the field and worth monitoring in the pre-race market, but the raw ability is obvious.
runners_data.comment: Merlin The Wizard brings back-to-back wins into this and has run over today's trip and going, yet he carries a testing 128 lb from stall 14 and an eighth two starts before those victories highlights some inconsistency in his recent record.

runners_data.name: Zaraahmando
runners_data.note: Trainer-jockey combination as Andrew Slattery does both jobs on this prominent type, who has a strikingly consistent run of placed efforts on Good ground over 8f; the form is reliable rather than spectacular but the style suits the expected shape and five days between runs is not a concern.
runners_data.comment: Zaraahmando is winless in his last six starts and, ranked 14th of 17 on our figures, is hard to fancy at the weights; that said, he has run over today's trip and going before, and back-to-back thirds suggest he keeps finding the frame.

runners_data.name: Calm The Jets
runners_data.note: A prominent racer with a ⚠ fade-in-finish tag who won over 8f on Standard 50 days ago but has run 9-8-0-8 on Good and Soft — the going has previously found this horse out and the finish-fade pattern is a direct hazard in a race that will likely test stamina in the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Calm The Jets won one from his last five starts, though two recent eighths and a ninth and an unplaced effort suggest consistency is the concern; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 123 lb from stall two, and 50 days off means fitness is also unproven.

runners_data.name: No More Porter
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness saddles this eight-year-old prominent type who has been remarkably consistent on Good ground (0W5P in similar conditions), with three runner-up finishes at 8f; the hg:tp headgear combination and five-day turnaround suggest fitness is not the issue — outright pace just eludes it.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, No More Porter has placed four times in that spell but also gone unplaced, and returning just five days after his latest effort raises freshness questions; he has run over today's trip and going, and the 122 lb burden from stall 11 adds little appeal at a ranking of 13 of 17.

runners_data.name: Tachos
runners_data.note: D K Weld's prominent racer has decent Good-ground placed form and wears headgear (tp); a 14-day break and Chris Hayes in the saddle add quality to the booking, but a record of 0W2P in similar conditions and a tendency to finish mid-pack limits the ceiling.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Tachos does arrive with experience of today's trip and going, yet a fifth last time out is her best recent effort and a draw of 17 gives her plenty to consider from the off.

runners_data.name: Java Wood
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good recently for K Smith and is a genuine prominent racer — but the field's pace density has pushed it into a midfield map position it will resist from the gates; if Wesley Joyce (3lb claim) can manoeuvre forward early the horse has the form to be competitive, though racing against its nature costs it.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Java Wood is hard to fancy at these weights, though he does boast a win two starts back and has run over today's trip and going before — small consolation from stall ten after a 48-day absence.

runners_data.name: San Aer
runners_data.note: This eight-year-old hold-up horse for Ross O'Sullivan has a single placed effort from nine Good-ground runs recently, ran just two days ago, and the redistribution into midfield reflects how crowded the back of this race is; a 0W1P record in similar conditions tells an honest story.
runners_data.comment: San Aer has run over today's distance and going before, and an 88 rating — ranking him second of 17 — suggests he's significantly better than his official mark of 70 implies; the concern is that he's winless in his last five starts, so converting that promise into results remains the challenge.

runners_data.name: Cala Bonita
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer for Matthew J Smith whose recent form includes a 4th over 13f on Good, suggesting stamina rather than pace is the engine; pushed back on the map due to congestion, and if Leigh Roche cannot find a forward position early, the horse will be racing in unfamiliar territory against its instincts.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 16 of 17 on our figures, Cala Bonita has been largely disappointing in recent starts — two eighths sandwiching a pair of fourths since winning five starts back — and her profile makes her tough to fancy, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns fit enough on a 14-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Vega's Muse is the sole confirmed front-runner and is expected to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the gates over this flat 1m½f on Good turf at Galway — with no genuine pace rivals willing or able to challenge for the lead, the fractions should be controlled and relatively honest rather than frantic. Behind her, a cluster of prominent types including Hygge, Molto Amichi, Zaraahmando, No More Porter, Tachos and Calm The Jets will jostle for position in the first few furlongs, though this field carries more pace than the map can accommodate — Java Wood and Cala Bonita are natural prominent horses who are likely to find themselves shuffled into midfield against their instincts, unable to secure their preferred berth. The hold-up brigade — Pink Oxalis, Tolebi, Glyndwr, Follow Me, Exquisite Acclaim, Earls, Merlin The Wizard and San Aer — will settle in behind a genuinely congested middle section, and with a lone front-runner setting a measured tempo, those who can travel prominently in the slipstream and sustain their effort into the straight will hold a clear positional advantage. This race shape most favours prominent-to-midfield racers with a turn of foot and Good-ground class — true hold-up horses face an additional burden of traffic and cover on a flat course where sustained grinding passages do not naturally open up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Vega's Muse Controls, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Vega's Muse leads uncontested at a genuine but manageable clip and the prominent holders time their challenge perfectly into the straight.
scenarios.body: Vega's Muse dictates a steady-to-fair pace and those sitting a length or two off her back — principally Hygge and Molto Amichi — are ideally positioned to pounce two furlongs out without burning petrol chasing the leader down. On Good ground on this flat course, the ability to race handily and kick from a close-up position is the decisive edge, and both Hygge (in-form, recent winner) and Molto Amichi (recent course winner) have the profile to deliver exactly that.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow in the early stages and horses from the upper-midfield range produce a sustained late run that swamps the prominent tier.
scenarios.body: A dawdling gallop set by Vega's Muse compresses the field and leaves multiple closers with a genuine shot at overhauling the leaders in the final furlong as the pace picks up sharply and the front-runners flatten out. Merlin The Wizard, despite being redistributed from his natural hold-up spot, has the raw form (two recent wins) and Good-ground class to be dangerous if gaps appear, while Earls — a three-time runner-up in similar conditions — profiles as the dogged finisher who capitalises when the prominent horses cry enough.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Overcrowd, Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the jostling among the large prominent contingent creates a messy early-to-mid race and a fresh hold-up horse finds a clear passage to arrive with a clean run.
scenarios.body: With Java Wood, Cala Bonita, Zaraahmando, No More Porter and Tachos all competing for similar ground, traffic incidents and interference between furlongs three and five are plausible, and a horse that has been kept out of trouble could arrive late with momentum others have spent. Glyndwr, racing just seven days after his last run but handled efficiently by Ben Coen, or Pink Oxalis — who has the Good-ground course form — could be the unexpected beneficiaries if a gap materialises late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Java Wood Or Cala Bonita Gate-Crash The Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Java Wood or Cala Bonita break sharply and override their redistributed mapping to push forward and force a faster pace than Vega's Muse intended to set.
scenarios.body: Both are natural prominent types who have been mapped back by congestion, and if either forces their way to the front the pace dynamic changes materially — a faster early tempo would string the field out and potentially compromise Vega's Muse's ability to control matters. In that altered scenario, horses with high cruising speed who can handle a proper gallop — Molto Amichi and Zaraahmando, both with multiple Good-ground placed efforts at this trip — would be best placed to benefit from the improved test of stamina.

watchPoints.text: Merlin The Wizard ran just two days ago — watch for any market drift that might signal connections are managing a quick turnaround rather than chasing the win; if supported, the back-to-back form is electric.

Calm The Jets carries a confirmed fade-in-finish flag on Good ground and races from a prominent position — if it blazes into the race early behind Vega's Muse and weakens inside the final furlong, it will severely interfere with hold-up horses trying to pick their way through.

Java Wood and Cala Bonita are both natural prominent types forced wide on the pace map — watch the first furlong to see whether either overrides the mapping and pushes forward aggressively, which would materially change the tempo for the entire field.

Vega's Muse holds a STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) suggesting it does not always lead — if it settles off the pace rather than making the running, the race loses its only confirmed front-runner and the early stages could become a tactical crawl with no horse prepared to take control.

Hygge's trainer Gordon Elliott has posted a 4/30 T14 strike rate — active but not at a peak clip; confirm the horse loads and travels smoothly, as a strong market move on race day would indicate Elliott's camp is particularly sweet on this assignment.

races.paceDynamic: Oust is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 21-runner field and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the gate, should secure a comfortable lead and dictate a controlled, even gallop over the 1m4f trip on Good ground at Galway. The pace will be honest but not brutal — a single pace-setter setting his own rhythm typically produces a mid-race lull before the tempo lifts in the final quarter-mile, compressing the finish. Several horses labelled prominent or hold-up in the data — including Berto Ramirez, Western Bandit, Rodeo Blues, and Day Trader — are redistributed to midfield because the sheer number of genuine hold-up types cannot all occupy the rear; the field holds more closers than the map can honestly place at the back, and Autumn Twist, Annie's Angel, Baila Conmigo, and Faro Island are the prominent types most likely to actually slot into the first half-dozen. This shape — a single uncontested leader, a bunched midfield, and a compressed finish on a flat, fair track — strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the pace and pounce, rather than true hold-up horses who will need a strong end-to-end gallop that Oust is unlikely to supply.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Oust bowls along unchallenged and the race is run at a steady-to-fair clip, allowing those just off the pace to strike at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Autumn Twist, Baila Conmigo, Faro Island, and Annie's Angel are ideally placed tracking Oust and can quicken into the straight without cover concerns; the controlled pace suits those with a turn of foot over staying the trip rather than grinders. Prominent racers who have shown good form on Good ground at this trip are the primary beneficiaries of this dominant shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Surge Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly stronger than expected mid-race, opening a gap that genuine hold-up horses can close late.
scenarios.body: Rodeo Blues and Jujubella both carry strong recent form and, if the tempo is sufficient in the final five furlongs, they can pick off rivals from behind; Rodeo Blues in particular has back-to-back wins and thrives on Good ground at this trip range. This shape requires a truer gallop than Oust alone is likely to generate, making it the second-most likely outcome but notably dependent on circumstances.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Oust Outstays The Field
scenarios.trigger: If Oust dictates so freely that the field is strung out and no prominent horse finds the pace to mount a sustained challenge.
scenarios.body: A 3-year-old carrying only 129lbs with a clear lead and a flat track could simply find the fuel to last home if the gallop is too compressed for closers to mobilise; horses in behind may lose rhythm in traffic in a large field, gifting Oust a wire-to-wire result. The style-fit caveat on Oust is noted, but the weight advantage and solo lead are genuine compensating factors.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Mayhem, Outsider Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the large 21-runner field causes interference, bunching, and positional chaos that scrambles normal outcomes.
scenarios.body: In a field this size on a flat track, a horse who finds a seam of daylight from an unexpected position — such as Showyoutheropes or Nancee Spain — can benefit from the carnage ahead; recent form on Good ground and a horse carrying little weight finding an unobstructed run could deliver a shock result. This scenario is low-probability but structurally plausible given the redistribution of so many hold-up types into the same midfield segment.

watchPoints.text: Oust (front-runner) carries only 129lbs with a 7lb claim — if he gets a completely uncontested lead and the field idles behind, he may not be caught; watch whether any prominent horse pushes forward to pressure him in the first half-mile.

The 21-runner field with a large cluster of hold-up types redistributed into the same midfield segment creates serious traffic risk in the straight — horses like Berto Ramirez, Western Bandit, Rodeo Blues, and Day Trader will all be hunting the same gap at the same time.
Dark Summit and Rhythm King both ran within the last 2 days — monitor market moves and any late withdrawals, as fatigue could cause erratic mid-race movement that disrupts runners around them.

Rodeo Blues (Joseph O'Brien, T14: 16/67) carries strong recent form and a powerful stable behind him; if the market shortens him significantly pre-race, the yard's confidence in getting a position from midfield in a big field should be respected.

Faro Island's combination of W J Lee booking, cheekpieces, and a positive form trajectory at this trip on Good ground makes him a key horse to watch in the early stages — if he slots into a prominent position smoothly, he becomes the benchmark for the Scenario A pace map.
